newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices ease 1/8 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices ease 1/8 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds edged down 1/8 point in late trade on Friday, though the supply shortfall helped muni futures continue to outperform Treasury bonds, which sagged on selling by hedge funds.
"The (municipal) contract is up a couple of ticks, but the cash market does not feel as good right now," a trader said.
Another trader estimated the losses in the long-end at around one or two basis points.

Trading was slowing ahead of the three-day U.S. Memorial Day holiday, and the amount of new issues that come to market next week was expected to fall about $1 billion to just over $2 billion, according to preliminary estimates.
During the week of May 27, the biggest negotiated offering is a nearly $144 million sale of revenue bonds by Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport, Texas.
On the competitive side, Los Angeles County MTA is selling almost $256 million of revenue bonds, while the District of Colombia plans to tap the market for nearly $244 million of general obligations.

While new issues were considered by traders to have gone smoothly this week, activity in the secondary market stayed pretty light. "I just think the cashflow is not there," a trader said. Later, he added: "Absolute levels are pretty high right now. They just want to take a breather."
A couple of mutual funds sent out bidwanted lists that, along with a few smaller lists, added up to as much as $200 million.

In the cash market, Treasury bonds perched just below the key seven percent level, losing 10 ticks to 95-15/32. Whether the bonds stay below that yield is considered a major test, and it absorbed much of participants' attention.
June municipal bond futures firmed four ticks to 116-10/32, while the June Treasury bond futures fell seven ticks to 109-2/32, leaving the MOB spread at plus 232 ticks.
In the secondary market, Dade County, Florida, Water and Sewer System Revenues of 2026, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.68 percent, NET, up two basis points.
And Florida Ports Financing Commission Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.80 percent NET, up one basis point.
